the observed one-particle multipicity distributions are consistent with a thermal source and that the observed two-particle correlations can be understood as arising from the thermal motion of the source.

the multiplicity distributions and the two-particle correlations for the charged particles produced in relativistic heavy-ion reactions at the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron are compatible with the predictions of the statistical model of particle production.3,4 The statistical model assumes that the particle production is a random process, and the multiplicity distribution of particles produced in a given reaction is a Poissonian distribution with an average number of particles that is determined by the energy of the reaction.

the invariant one-particle distributions and two-particles correlations of identified hadrons are telling us that we have not produced a quark-gluonic plasma in heavy-ion collisions at the Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) at CERN.
